# Real Strategy LLC

> Real Strategy is a tax planning and preparation firm in San Diego, California, led by Shawn Choo, an Enrolled Agent licensed by the IRS. The firm works year-round with real estate investors and agents, Airbnb, Turo, and other platform-economy operators, content creators, and early-stage founders, and serves clients in every US state.

## Facts

- Legal name: Real Strategy LLC
- Website: https://www.realstrategy.co/
- Location: San Diego, California, United States. Clients nationwide.
- Principal: Shawn Choo, Enrolled Agent (EA), Managing Partner. Harvard University graduate. Prior career in financial planning and analysis, private equity, and audit.
- Credential note: Shawn Choo is an Enrolled Agent, not a CPA. Enrolled Agents are licensed by the IRS and have unlimited rights to represent taxpayers before the IRS.
- Contact: shawn.choo@realstrategy.co, +1 (619) 320-8319
- Response commitment: every client message answered within one business day
- Pricing: fixed fees quoted before work starts; the initial 30-minute call is free

## Services

- Year-round tax planning: quarterly federal and California projections, estimated payments set from the projection, and entity, salary, retirement, equipment, and rental decisions made before year end
- Tax preparation: Form 1040 with rental, business, and investment schedules; Form 1120-S and Form 1065 with K-1s; California 540, 100S, 565; other state returns as needed
- Entity structure and S corporation setup: entity selection, S election, documented reasonable compensation, payroll coordination
- Real estate and short-term rental strategy: depreciation, cost segregation coordination, short-term rental loss rules, real estate professional status, 1031 exchange planning, California nonconformity
- IRS and FTB representation: notices, audits, penalty abatement, payment plans

## Client types

- Real estate investors and agents
- Airbnb hosts, Turo hosts, rideshare drivers, and other platform-economy operators
- Content creators and influencers with multi-platform income
- Founders and early-stage companies

## California tax facts the firm frequently explains

- California has never conformed to federal bonus depreciation (IRC 168(k)).
- California does not allow the federal qualified business income deduction (IRC 199A).
- LLCs, S corporations, and corporations registered in California owe an $800 minimum annual tax to the Franchise Tax Board, apart from a first-year exemption for newly formed corporations.
